subject.title: [Bug]: In msteams channel messages, OpenClaw can't access inbound attachments

question: Should the Microsoft Teams Graph media fallback be opt-in via `channels.msteams.graphMediaFallback`, enabled broadly for channel/group messages, or redesigned around a narrower detection signal before landing a fix?
rationale: Current main preserves the earlier mention-only Graph-noise protection, but live evidence shows that same gate prevents real inbound file attachments from reaching the agent when Teams strips attachment markers; the fix changes network behavior and possibly config surface.

options.title: Land config-gated fallback
options.body: Review and finish https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101096 so existing deployments keep the current default and affected operators opt in to the extra Graph lookup.

options.title: Land broad channel fix
options.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90738 if maintainers accept broader default Graph fallback attempts to cover the original channel root causes.

options.title: Require a different signal
options.body: Keep this issue open while designing a non-config way to distinguish file stubs from mention-only HTML without reintroducing noisy Graph lookups.

recommendation.title: Land config-gated fallback
recommendation.body: Review and finish https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101096 so existing deployments keep the current default and affected operators opt in to the extra Graph lookup.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest feature-history signal across Teams plugin ownership and attachment-flow hardening, and this choice is about product/config tradeoff rather than a single line repair.
